newsitem.title: UK: UK water utility shares fall on price-cut fears.
newsitem.headline: UK water utility shares fall on price-cut fears.

text.p: Shares in Britain's water utilities sank on Wednesday after industry regulator Ofwat said customers should expect price cuts at the next periodic review which will be completed in December 1999.

By 0811 GMT in pre-market trade, Thames Water Plc was marked down seven pence to 658 while Severn Trent Plc fell eight pence to 713, South West Water Plc dropped 6-1/2p to 670 and United Utilities Plc lost 5-1/2p to 677.
"All the water shares have been marked down on the back of the regulator's statement," one market-maker said.
Ofwat said in a statement that one of its main objectives for the price review was that cost savings made by water companies since the last review in 1994 should be quickly transferred to customers.

"At the next review I will expect companies to demonstrate improving standards for their customers and efficiency gains will allow prices to come down in real terms, despite continuing capital investment requirements," Ofwat head Ian Byatt said.
